#Stats per cell
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
Stats_intestine <- read.csv("/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Pool32/Combi/stats/stats_intestine.csv", header = T, sep = ",")
ano_intestine_combi <- read.table("/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Pool32/Combi/stats/Pool32B_NPC_cell_stats.tsv", header = T, sep = "\t")
ano_intestine_combi$condition <- "48h_Dox"


d <- density(log10(ano_intestine_combi$readcount), na.rm = TRUE)
y <- d$y
x <- d$x

# Find where slope changes from decreasing to increasing (i.e., local minima)
valley_indices <- which(diff(sign(diff(y))) == 2) + 1

# Get valleys around x ≈ 3.5 to 4.5 (just before the second peak)
target_valleys <- valley_indices[x[valley_indices] > 3.5 & x[valley_indices] < 4.5]

# Extract the most likely valley
cutoff_point <- x[target_valleys[which.min(y[target_valleys])]]
print(paste("Cutoff at local minimum:", round(cutoff_point, 3)))

cutoff_index <- target_valleys[which.min(y[target_valleys])]
cutoff_x <- x[cutoff_index]
cutoff_y <- y[cutoff_index]

# Plot
ggplot(data = data.frame(x = x, y = y), aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_line(color = "#377EB8", size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff_x, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = cutoff_x, y = cutoff_y), color = "red", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = cutoff_x, y = cutoff_y + 0.0005,
           label = paste0("Cutoff ≈ ", round(cutoff_x, 2)),
           color = "red", vjust = -2, hjust = -0.10, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "48h Dox",
    x = "log10(Annotated Reads)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
       theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain",colour = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(size =11, face = "plain", hjust = 0.5,colour = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain", hjust = 1,colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain",colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.2, "cm"),   # overall size
    legend.key.width = unit(0.2, "cm"),  # width
    legend.key.height = unit(0.2, "cm"))+
    guides(fill= guide_legend(nrow = 1))

ggsave("/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Thesis/chapter_2/Plots/Figure2/local_minima_histogram_combi_intestine_plus.png", dpi=300, width = 3.5, height = 2)
ggsave("/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Thesis/chapter_2/Plots/Figure2/illustrator/local_minima_histogram_combi_intestine_plus.pdf", dpi=300, width = 3.5, height = 2)

ano_intestine_combi_sub <- ano_intestine_combi[log10(ano_intestine_combi$readcount) > 4.45,]



```

```{r}
Stats_intestine <- read.csv("/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Pool32/Combi/stats/stats_intestine.csv", header = T, sep = ",")

# Plot
```

```{r}
batch_list3 <- readRDS(file = "/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Pool_35/Harber/Large_harber_plate_integration/Atlas_Large_plates_RNA_DCM_list.rds")

batch_list4$DCM_plate <- NULL
batch_list4$DCM_combi <- combi_intestine_seurat

batch_list4 <- lapply(batch_list4, function(obj) {
  obj <- NormalizeData(obj)
  obj <- FindVariableFeatures(obj, selection.method = "vst")
  return(obj)
})

# Find integration anchors (takes time for large datasets)
integration_features <- SelectIntegrationFeatures(object.list = batch_list4)
anchors <- FindIntegrationAnchors(
  object.list = batch_list4,
  anchor.features = integration_features,
  dims = 1:15  # Adjust based on your PCA results
)

integrated_seurat_combi <- IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors, dims = 1:15, k.weight = 70)

# Switch to integrated assay (important!)
DefaultAssay(integrated_seurat_combi) <- "integrated"

# Scale data and run PCA
integrated_seurat_combi <- ScaleData(integrated_seurat_combi)
integrated_seurat_combi <- RunPCA(integrated_seurat_combi, npcs = 50)

# Check batch effect correction (batches should mix well in PCA)
DimPlot(integrated_seurat_combi, reduction = "pca", group.by = "orig.ident")
```

##Module score by integrated gene markers

```{r}
integrated_seurat_combi_markers_sub<- integrated_seurat_combi_markers_sub[integrated_seurat_combi_markers_sub$avg_log2FC > 0.5,]
unique_clusters <- unique(integrated_seurat_combi_markers_sub$cluster)

# Create an empty list to store the final plots for each cluster
plus_fplots <- list()

# Iterate over each cluster
for (cluster in unique_clusters) {
  # Individual module
  #module <- intersected_genes_by_cluster[[cluster]]
  module <- integrated_seurat_combi_markers_sub[integrated_seurat_combi_markers_sub$cluster == cluster, "gene"]

  # Add module scores to the gast object
  integrated_seurat_combi <- AddModuleScore( integrated_seurat_combi, features = list(c(module)), name = paste0(cluster),  nbin = 5)
  
  # Generate the feature plot for the current cluster
  plus_fplot <- FeaturePlot(object =  integrated_seurat_combi, reduction = "umap",features = paste0(cluster, "1"), pt.size = 0.5, cols= c("white","#B0B0B0", "#882255"))
  #scale_colour_gradientn(colours = rev(brewer.pal(n = 11, name = "RdBu")))
  
  # Save the plot to the plus_fplots list
  plus_fplots[[paste0("plus_fplot", cluster)]] <- plus_fplot
  
  # Save the plots
  ggsave(filename = paste0("/media/erlantz/71DE167A75E99BB4/Thesis/chapter_2/Plots/Figure2/", cluster, "_markers_integrated_MS.png"), plot = plus_fplot, dpi = 300,width = 5, height = 3)

}

# Filter for Combi_DCM
df <- subset(plot_df_long, dataset == "sciMeDseq")

# Prepare an empty list to collect plots
plots <- list()

# Loop through clusters
for (clust in unique(df$cluster)) {
  
  df_clust <- df %>% filter(cluster == clust)
  
  # Target identity to compare against
  ref_group <- clust  # assuming cluster names match cell_identity_int exactly
  
  # Skip cluster if reference group not present
  if (!(ref_group %in% df_clust$cell_identity_int2)) next
  
  # Create pairwise comparisons: each group vs the cluster's reference group
  identities <- unique(df_clust$cell_identity_int2)
  comparisons <- lapply(setdiff(identities, ref_group), function(other) c(ref_group, other))

  # Add highlight column
  df_clust <- df_clust %>%
    mutate(highlight = ifelse(cell_identity_int2 == ref_group, "Target", "Rest"))
  
  # Plot
  p <- ggplot(df_clust, aes(x = cell_identity_int2, y = module_score, fill = highlight)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = ,
      x = "",
      y = paste0("DCM Z Module Score\n",clust)
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Target" = "#D55E00", "Rest" = "#0072B2")) +
    stat_compare_means(
      comparisons = comparisons,
      method = "wilcox.test",
      label = "p.signif",
      tip.length = 0.01
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25)))+
       theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain",colour = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(size =11, face = "plain", hjust = 0.5,colour = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, angle=45,face = "plain", hjust = 1,colour = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain", hjust = 1,colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain",colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.2, "cm"),   # overall size
    legend.key.width = unit(0.2, "cm"),  # width
    legend.key.height = unit(0.2, "cm"))+
    guides(fill= guide_legend(nrow = 1))

    p_nolegend <- p #+ theme(legend.position = "none")

  plots[[clust]] <- p_nolegend
}
```

```{r}
calculate_chunk_percentages <- function(df, chunk_size = 7) {
  percentages <- c()
  for (i in seq(1, nrow(df), by = chunk_size)) {
    chunk <- df[i:(i + chunk_size - 1), ]
    total <- sum(chunk$Freq)
    chunk_percentages <- if (total != 0) (chunk$Freq / total) * 100 else rep(0, chunk_size)
    percentages <- c(percentages, chunk_percentages)
  }
  return(percentages)
}

cell_annotation_integration_types$per <- calculate_chunk_percentages(cell_annotation_integration_types)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
Stats_intestine_chase <- read.csv("/media/erlantz/Erlantz/Pool_37_combi_chase/stats/Combi_chase_intestine_stats.csv", header = T, sep = ",")
ano_intestine_combi_chase <- read.table("/media/erlantz/Erlantz/Pool_37_combi_chase/stats/Combi_intestine_cell_stats.tsv", header = T, sep = "\t")
ano_intestine_combi_chase$condition <- "48h_Dox_72h_chase"


d <- density(log10(ano_intestine_combi_chase$readcount), na.rm = TRUE)
y <- d$y
x <- d$x

# Find where slope changes from decreasing to increasing (i.e., local minima)
valley_indices <- which(diff(sign(diff(y))) == 2) + 1

# Get valleys around x ≈ 3.5 to 4.5 (just before the second peak)
target_valleys <- valley_indices[x[valley_indices] > 3.5 & x[valley_indices] < 4.5]

# Extract the most likely valley
cutoff_point <- x[target_valleys[which.min(y[target_valleys])]]
print(paste("Cutoff at local minimum:", round(cutoff_point, 3)))

cutoff_index <- target_valleys[which.min(y[target_valleys])]
cutoff_x <- x[cutoff_index]
cutoff_y <- y[cutoff_index]

# Plot
ggplot(data = data.frame(x = x, y = y), aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_line(color = "#377EB8", size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff_x, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = cutoff_x, y = cutoff_y), color = "red", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = cutoff_x, y = cutoff_y + 0.0005,
           label = paste0("Cutoff ≈ ", round(cutoff_x, 2)),
           color = "red", vjust = -2, hjust = -0.10, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "48h Dox 72h Chase",
    x = "log10(Annotated Reads)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
       theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain",colour = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(size =11, face = "plain", hjust = 0.5,colour = "black"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain", hjust = 1,colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "plain",colour = "black"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.2, "cm"),   # overall size
    legend.key.width = unit(0.2, "cm"),  # width
    legend.key.height = unit(0.2, "cm"))+
    guides(fill= guide_legend(nrow = 1))

ggsave("/media/erlantz/Erlantz/Pool_37_combi_chase/Figures/local_minima_histogram_combi_intestine_chase.png", dpi=300, width = 3.5, height = 2)
```

```{r}
# Cluster proportion comparison between datasets
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(cowplot)
library(scales)
library(ggpubr)
library(fisher.test)

# ============================================================================
# MAIN FUNCTION: Calculate and compare cluster proportions
# ============================================================================

compare_cluster_proportions <- function(seurat_obj,
                                      group_by = "dataset",  # Column that defines your datasets
                                      cluster_col = "seurat_clusters",
                                      statistical_test = TRUE,
                                      plot_type = "all") {  # "all", "barplot", "dotplot", "heatmap"
  
  # Get metadata
  meta_data <- seurat_obj@meta.data
  
  # Check if columns exist
  if (!group_by %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
    stop(paste("Column", group_by, "not found in metadata"))
  }
  if (!cluster_col %in% colnames(meta_data)) {
    stop(paste("Column", cluster_col, "not found in metadata"))
  }
  
  # Calculate proportions
  prop_data <- meta_data %>%
    count(!!sym(group_by), !!sym(cluster_col), name = "n_cells") %>%
    group_by(!!sym(group_by)) %>%
    mutate(
      total_cells = sum(n_cells),
      proportion = n_cells / total_cells,
      percentage = proportion * 100
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Calculate overall statistics
  summary_stats <- prop_data %>%
    group_by(!!sym(cluster_col)) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_prop = mean(proportion),
      sd_prop = sd(proportion),
      mean_pct = mean(percentage),
      sd_pct = sd(percentage),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  # Statistical testing if requested
  stat_results <- NULL
  if (statistical_test) {
    stat_results <- perform_statistical_tests(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col)
  }
  
  # Create plots
  plots <- list()
  
  if (plot_type %in% c("all", "barplot")) {
    plots$barplot <- create_proportion_barplot(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col)
  }
  
  if (plot_type %in% c("all", "dotplot")) {
    plots$dotplot <- create_proportion_dotplot(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col)
  }
  
  if (plot_type %in% c("all", "heatmap")) {
    plots$heatmap <- create_proportion_heatmap(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col)
  }
  
  if (plot_type %in% c("all", "comparison")) {
    plots$comparison <- create_comparison_plot(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col)
  }
  
  # Combined plot
  if (plot_type == "all") {
    plots$combined <- plot_grid(
      plots$barplot, plots$dotplot,
      plots$heatmap, plots$comparison,
      ncol = 2, align = "hv",
      labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D")
    )
  }
  
  return(list(
    data = prop_data,
    summary = summary_stats,
    statistical_tests = stat_results,
    plots = plots
  ))
}

# ============================================================================
# PLOTTING FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

create_proportion_barplot <- function(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col) {
  p <- ggplot(prop_data, aes_string(x = cluster_col, y = "percentage", fill = group_by)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")), 
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
              vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      legend.position = "top",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Cluster Proportions by Dataset",
      x = "Cluster",
      y = "Percentage of Cells (%)",
      fill = "Dataset"
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1))
  
  return(p)
}

create_proportion_dotplot <- function(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col) {
  p <- ggplot(prop_data, aes_string(x = group_by, y = cluster_col)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = percentage, color = percentage), alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Percentage", range = c(2, 10)) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Percentage") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Cluster Proportions - Dot Plot",
      x = "Dataset",
      y = "Cluster"
    )
  
  return(p)
}

create_proportion_heatmap <- function(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col) {
  # Reshape data for heatmap
  heatmap_data <- prop_data %>%
    select(!!sym(group_by), !!sym(cluster_col), percentage) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = !!sym(group_by), values_from = percentage, values_fill = 0)
  
  # Convert to long format for ggplot
  heatmap_long <- heatmap_data %>%
    pivot_longer(-!!sym(cluster_col), names_to = group_by, values_to = "percentage")
  
  p <- ggplot(heatmap_long, aes_string(x = group_by, y = cluster_col, fill = "percentage")) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(percentage, 1), "%")), 
              color = ifelse(heatmap_long$percentage > 50, "white", "black"),
              size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Percentage") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Cluster Proportions - Heatmap",
      x = "Dataset",
      y = "Cluster"
    )
  
  return(p)
}

create_comparison_plot <- function(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col) {
  # Calculate fold changes if there are exactly 2 datasets
  datasets <- unique(prop_data[[group_by]])
  
  if (length(datasets) == 2) {
    # Calculate fold change
    wide_data <- prop_data %>%
      select(!!sym(group_by), !!sym(cluster_col), percentage) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = !!sym(group_by), values_from = percentage, values_fill = 0)
    
    wide_data$fold_change <- log2((wide_data[[datasets[2]]] + 0.1) / (wide_data[[datasets[1]]] + 0.1))
    wide_data$abs_fold_change <- abs(wide_data$fold_change)
    
    p <- ggplot(wide_data, aes_string(x = cluster_col, y = "fold_change")) +
      geom_col(aes(fill = fold_change > 0), alpha = 0.8) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
      geom_text(aes(label = round(fold_change, 2)), 
                vjust = ifelse(wide_data$fold_change > 0, -0.3, 1.3), size = 3) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "blue"),
                       labels = c("TRUE" = paste("Higher in", datasets[2]),
                                "FALSE" = paste("Higher in", datasets[1])),
                       name = "Enrichment") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Log2 Fold Change:", datasets[2], "vs", datasets[1]),
        x = "Cluster",
        y = "Log2 Fold Change"
      )
  } else {
    # For more than 2 datasets, create a line plot
    p <- ggplot(prop_data, aes_string(x = cluster_col, y = "percentage", color = group_by, group = group_by)) +
      geom_line(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.8) +
      geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "Cluster Proportions Across Datasets",
        x = "Cluster",
        y = "Percentage of Cells (%)",
        color = "Dataset"
      ) +
      scale_color_viridis_d() +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1))
  }
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================
# STATISTICAL TESTING
# ============================================================================

perform_statistical_tests <- function(prop_data, group_by, cluster_col) {
  # Get unique datasets and clusters
  datasets <- unique(prop_data[[group_by]])
  clusters <- unique(prop_data[[cluster_col]])
  
  if (length(datasets) < 2) {
    warning("Need at least 2 datasets for statistical testing")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Perform chi-square test for overall differences
  contingency_table <- prop_data %>%
    select(!!sym(group_by), !!sym(cluster_col), n_cells) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = !!sym(group_by), values_from = n_cells, values_fill = 0) %>%
    column_to_rownames(cluster_col) %>%
    as.matrix()
  
  # Overall chi-square test
  chisq_result <- chisq.test(contingency_table)
  
  # Pairwise comparisons for each cluster (if exactly 2 datasets)
  pairwise_results <- NULL
  if (length(datasets) == 2) {
    pairwise_results <- data.frame(
      cluster = character(),
      dataset1 = character(),
      dataset2 = character(),
      prop1 = numeric(),
      prop2 = numeric(),
      p_value = numeric(),
      significant = logical(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    for (clust in clusters) {
      clust_data <- prop_data[prop_data[[cluster_col]] == clust, ]
      
      if (nrow(clust_data) == 2) {  # Both datasets have this cluster
        # Fisher's exact test or proportion test
        n1 <- clust_data$n_cells[1]
        n2 <- clust_data$n_cells[2]
        total1 <- clust_data$total_cells[1]
        total2 <- clust_data$total_cells[2]
        
        # Two-proportion z-test
        prop_test <- prop.test(c(n1, n2), c(total1, total2))
        
        pairwise_results <- rbind(pairwise_results, data.frame(
          cluster = clust,
          dataset1 = datasets[1],
          dataset2 = datasets[2],
          prop1 = clust_data$proportion[1],
          prop2 = clust_data$proportion[2],
          p_value = prop_test$p.value,
          significant = prop_test$p.value < 0.05,
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        ))
      }
    }
  }
  
  return(list(
    overall_chisq = chisq_result,
    pairwise_tests = pairwise_results
  ))
}

# ============================================================================
# UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Function to add dataset information if not present
add_dataset_info <- function(seurat_obj, dataset_column, dataset_mapping) {
  # dataset_mapping should be a named vector: c("sample1" = "dataset1", "sample2" = "dataset1", ...)
  
  if (!"orig.ident" %in% colnames(seurat_obj@meta.data)) {
    stop("orig.ident column not found. Cannot map datasets.")
  }
  
  seurat_obj@meta.data[[dataset_column]] <- dataset_mapping[seurat_obj@meta.data$orig.ident]
  
  return(seurat_obj)
}

# Function to create summary table
create_summary_table <- function(comparison_result) {
  summary_table <- comparison_result$data %>%
    select(dataset = 1, cluster = 2, n_cells, total_cells, percentage) %>%
    arrange(cluster, dataset)
  
  return(summary_table)
}
```
